question: 在 Google Gemini CLI 官方公开文档、源码和测试中，跨重启/崩溃/断电后的 session history 恢复、历史保留与清理、工具调用恢复及审计证据边界分别被证明到什么程度？重点是 crash/power-loss、恢复后的 dangling tool call 与 resume 后重试安全性。

excluded: S1-S18 directories and local research artifacts

claims.claim: Checkpointing is created before an approved filesystem-modifying tool and stores a shadow Git snapshot, conversation history, and the tool call; /restore restores local files/history and re-proposes the original tool call.

sources.support: Official documentation explicitly lists Git snapshot, conversation history, tool call, and restore/re-propose behavior.

claims.caveat: This is a local pre-modification checkpoint workflow, not proof of crash/power-loss automatic recovery.

claims.claim: Checkpointing is disabled by default and enabled through settings.json; the --checkpointing flag was removed in version 0.11.0.

sources.support: Official configuration section states default disabled and settings.json enablement.

claims.caveat: Configuration documentation does not establish durability after power loss.

claims.claim: Normal session resume is exposed through --resume/-r and /resume, restoring saved chat history and allowing session browsing.

sources.support: Official tutorial describes --resume/-r, restored chat history/memory, /resume browser, and loading a selected session.

claims.caveat: A resume entry point is not proof that every interrupted tool is automatically replayed.

claims.claim: Manual deletion paths include /resume browser deletion, --delete-session, and /exit --delete; exit deletion removes conversation history and tool output files.

sources.support: Official session management tutorial documents all listed deletion operations.

claims.caveat: These documented paths do not establish retention behavior for every checkpoint or remote log.

claims.claim: The settings reference gives session retention defaults of enabled=true and maxAge=30d.

sources.support: Official settings table lists Enable Session Cleanup default true and Keep chat history default 30d.

claims.caveat: This is the documented setting default; filesystem availability and user overrides remain separate.

claims.claim: Startup session cleanup scans chats, deletes corrupted files, applies maxAge/maxCount based on lastUpdated, and excludes the current active session from deletable sessions; official tests cover these behaviors.

sources.support: Implementation calls cleanup during startup, identifies corrupted/expired sessions, sorts by lastUpdated, excludes current session, and cleans artifacts.
Official integration tests assert disabled/no-directory behavior, old session deletion, current/recent retention, and subagent cleanup.

claims.caveat: Cleanup concerns local session files and associated artifacts; it is not evidence of crash recovery or a universal retention policy for all data.

claims.claim: ToolCallRecord supports id, name, args, optional/null result, status, timestamp, and optional agent/display fields; status values include validating, scheduled, executing, awaiting_approval, success, error, and cancelled.

sources.support: Official type definition makes result optional/null and status required.
Official scheduler enum defines the call lifecycle statuses.

claims.caveat: A recorded status/result is local evidence of recording, not proof of external side-effect state.

claims.claim: Completed tool calls are recorded with request name/args, response parts when available, status, timestamp, and are merged by call ID into the Gemini message.

sources.support: Official ChatRecordingService/GeminiChat code constructs completed records and updates existing records by tool call id.

claims.caveat: The source does not define a crash-time transaction spanning tool execution and recording.

claims.claim: Session recording appends JSONL records synchronously and has a fallback that preserves an unreadable file and atomically rewrites a clean file from in-memory conversation; no explicit fsync or power-loss guarantee is shown.

sources.support: Official implementation uses appendFileSync for lines and temp-file rename in rewriteConversationFile; no fsync is present in the cited path.

claims.caveat: Absence in this code path is not proof that no platform/filesystem durability exists elsewhere.

claims.claim: Checkpoint utility data includes history, clientHistory, tool name/args, commitHash, and messageId; missing file_path causes the restorable tool call to be skipped.

sources.support: Official checkpoint utility constructs the data structure and tests fallback/skip behavior.

claims.caveat: This is checkpoint creation/restoration data, not an automatic replay protocol.

claims.claim: A process termination between recording stages could leave a stored tool call with no result or an intermediate status; this is allowed by the model and append structure but is not an officially crash-tested replay semantic.

sources.support: Tool calls are appended/merged and results are optional in the record type; inference is limited to possible persisted shapes.

claims.caveat: No permitted official test was found that kills the process at each boundary or proves the resulting state after restart.

claims.claim: Because /restore re-proposes the original tool call, repeating a call can carry duplicate-side-effect risk unless the tool/external system is idempotent; official material does not establish exactly-once or remote deduplication.

sources.support: Official docs state that restore re-proposes the original tool call; no exactly-once or deduplication statement accompanies it.

claims.caveat: Risk is a safety inference, not evidence that a duplicate actually occurred.

claims.claim: Automatic recovery after crash or power loss to the last consistent point is proven by the official public materials.
claims.caveat: Unknown: the allowed snapshot/docs/tests did not provide a crash/power-loss durability proof or test.

claims.claim: Gemini CLI provides exactly-once execution, deduplication, or a safe automatic retry protocol for resumed tool calls.
claims.caveat: Unknown: no official exactly-once, idempotency-key, or remote deduplication contract was found.

claims.claim: Restoring a checkpoint rolls back remote side effects or proves their absence.
claims.caveat: Unknown: official checkpoint docs describe local files, shadow Git, history, and tool re-proposal only.

claims.claim: Checkpoint files, shadow Git snapshots, tool-output artifacts, and remote logs all obey the same documented retention period.
claims.caveat: Unknown: session cleanup implementation documents/implements session and associated local artifacts, not a universal retention contract for every evidence store.

claims.claim: Production validation of crash recovery, dangling-call repair, exactly-once behavior, or remote rollback was performed by this research.
claims.caveat: Inaccessible by scope: no real services, credentials, or production systems were accessed; this report makes no such claim.

not_found_or_unverified: automatic dangling tool call recovery contract
coverage.next_slice: S20: isolated fault-injection matrix for local JSONL append, checkpoint write, tool execution boundary, and resume/restore observability without real remote side effects.
